editorial: Topper Returns is a 1941 American film, the third in the Topper series. The print's US status is not settled. No renewal was found in the parts of the 1968 and 1969 Catalog of Copyright Entries Motion Pictures volumes that could be read, but the renewal sections were not reached and the film's original registration date was not found. Treat the print as unconfirmed until the registration date is found and the full renewal volumes are searched by hand. Separate layers are also open: the underlying source characters, any pre-existing music in the track, and any restored copy, which could add new titles or other material.

Does a restored copy have its own copyright?

A faithful restoration adds no new US copyright in the film itself. Anything the restorers added, such as new titles, a new score or other new material, could be protected. I could not confirm any specific restoration of this film, so check what a given copy adds before copying from it.
